modules.name: engine (outer seam)
modules.responsibility: Owns the host-facing RenderEngine: input queue, show/graph resolution, action execution into a voice pool, envelope ticking, compositing, and telemetry.
modules.notes: 6-method interface over ~700 lines of class body with ~20 mutable private maps (seqIndex, lastPick, latched, mixMemberSnapshots, cc/osc/note tables, pendingFires, renderPlanCache). Deepest module in scope but also the biggest single-file concentration of state; applyInput is ~400 lines (298-694).

modules.name: eval-graph
modules.responsibility: Pure evaluator that walks a compiled trigger graph for one pad hit and emits Play/Stop/Pending actions.
modules.notes: evalGraphGen3FromPlan spans lines 277-594 — a single ~320-line recursive traversal with per-NodeKind branching. EvalState is a bag of caller-owned maps handed in by the engine (shared mutable seam).

modules.name: voice types & show model
modules.responsibility: Central type vocabulary for the voice-bus domain: Show, Bus, EffectDef, Preset, TriggerGraph nodes/edges, envelopes, params, play modes.
modules.notes: Type-only module plus two small helpers; ~43 exported names. It is the shared vocabulary every other voice module imports, so widening it is the cheapest way to leak concepts.

modules.name: compositor (inner seam)
modules.responsibility: Renders the live voice list into a destination framebuffer — additive accumulation, mix scratch buffers, per-voice effective-param resolution.
modules.notes: Small interface (one render method) over the perf hotspot; closure-captured scratch buffers. applyEffectiveParams is exported separately and also called by the engine — a second entry point into the same logic.

modules.name: generator-bridge
modules.responsibility: Adapts a voice into a RenderContext for a hosted EffectGenerator, choosing absolute vs voice-local clock and owning per-voice generator state.
modules.notes: The only place voice-world meets effects-world. Reads EffectGenerator.timebase; owns state lifecycle (create/reset).

modules.name: voice pool & lifecycle
modules.responsibility: Fixed-slab object pool for Voice records plus the per-frame envelope advance and dead-voice reap.
modules.notes: Pool is deep (allocation discipline behind acquire/release); envelope-tick is two free functions taking the pool array plus a busById map — a procedure, not an abstraction.

modules.name: render-plan compiler
modules.responsibility: Compiles a TriggerGraph into a cached, traversal-ready RenderPlan with node categories, flow children, and structural issues.
modules.notes: Cache keyed on a string signature — correctness depends on the signature covering every field traversal reads.

modules.name: graph integrity & normalization
modules.responsibility: Normalizes legacy graphs to the Gen3 shape and validates structural integrity, reporting coded issues or throwing.
modules.notes: A migration layer plus a guard in one file; the migration path is legacy-shaped and likely to outlive its need.

modules.name: graph lints
modules.responsibility: Read-only static analyses over a trigger graph reporting empty-scope targets and unreachable nodes for the authoring UI.
modules.notes: Two sibling analyses with the same shape (graph in, issue list out) but no shared lint framing.

modules.name: modulation core
modules.responsibility: Defines modulation sources (envelope/lfo/cc/note/osc/random), samples them, and applies mappings to base parameter values.
modules.notes: cc/osc/note each get their own near-identical key/value01/sample trio. modulation-parity.ts is a legacy-vs-new comparison harness living in production source and re-exported from index.

modules.name: envelopes & easing
modules.responsibility: Envelope shapes (preset kinds, ADSR, custom point curves) with sampling, cloning, migration, and the shared easing function table.
modules.notes: `ease(spec, t)` is a clean deep seam; envelope.ts mixes sampling with schema migration (migrateAdsr).

modules.name: scope resolution
modules.responsibility: Parses and intersects drum/kit/hoop scope targets into concrete pixel-range targets with configurable empty-hoop fallback.
modules.notes: EmptyHoopFallback ('first'|'sentinel'|'none') is a caller-supplied policy knob — a place different callers can disagree.

modules.name: determinism primitives
modules.responsibility: Seeded RNG, musical delay-division→ms conversion, and LFO waveform sampling — the deterministic time/randomness substrate.
modules.notes: Leaf modules, no intra-scope deps; the purity guarantee of the whole engine rests here.

modules.name: modifier graph
modules.responsibility: Resolves modifier nodes and chains attached to a play node into a single ResolvedModifier applied at spawn.
modules.notes: Two functions, one of which loops the other; thin over the node data it reads.

modules.name: diagnostics
modules.responsibility: Type vocabulary for engine diagnostic events (graph resolution path, miss reasons, sink callback).
modules.notes: Pure types + a callback alias; the seam it defines is real, the module is a declaration file.

modules.name: voice public barrel
modules.responsibility: Curates the package-facing export surface for the voice subsystem, mixing blanket re-exports with hand-picked named ones.
modules.notes: Inconsistent policy: `export *` for 8 modules, explicit lists for 8 others; exports test-support material (MODULATION_PARITY_CASES) as public API.

modules.name: effect generator contract
modules.responsibility: Defines the EffectGenerator interface, param spec vocabulary, timebase flag, and tolerant param readers.
modules.notes: The contract all 49 effects implement; deliberately narrow (render + optional createState). Note there is a SECOND unrelated `ParamSpec` in voice/types.ts.

modules.name: effect registry & taxonomy
modules.responsibility: Assembles all built-in generators into a keyed registry, merges central metadata, resolves retired ids, and derives play-type collections from tags.
modules.notes: Registry is shallow (a Map with three accessors) but carries the metadata-merge and canvas-fallback policy; the 49 imports + 49-entry ALL array is a hand-maintained parallel list. Module-level `throw` on duplicate id and an import side effect ('../canvas/presets').

modules.name: emitter (hit-emission substrate)
modules.responsibility: Per-hit emission list with aging, TTL expiry, capped spawn, and per-emission payload — the shared spine of the emission-based effects.
modules.notes: Used by 7 of 49 effects (chase-bands, drum-sonar, gravity-drops, orbit-comet, ripple-3d, scan-plane, spark-arc). The rest re-derive hit tracking themselves.

modules.name: effect implementations
modules.responsibility: Forty-nine concrete pure pixel generators covering base looks, hit effects, 2D UV textures, particles, and meters.
public_interface: one exported const EffectGenerator per file (solidBase, chase, plasma, sparkArc, …)
modules.notes: Each file is data (id/name/paramSpec/tags) plus one render loop; 49/49 import color, 38 import math. Individually shallow by design — the depth lives in the shared contract and helpers.

modules.name: effects test suite
modules.responsibility: Per-effect behavioural coverage sharded into lettered batches plus registry/alias/vocabulary contract tests.
modules.notes: jscpd's largest clone cluster lives here: the batch-* files repeat the same model/framebuffer/ctx setup per effect. The batch split appears arbitrary (letters, not concepts).

seams.why: Six-method host boundary with a NullEngine already implementing it — behaviour swappable without touching hosts.
Voices→pixels is a one-method interface; an alternate compositor drops in without engine edits.
New visual behaviour is added by writing a new object against this contract, never by editing the render path.

Adding an effect requires editing two places in this file (import + array) plus optionally metadata.ts — the extension point is a hand-maintained list, not a registration call. tryGetEffect also hardcodes the canvas fallback.
Single adapter point between the voice world and the effects world; timebase policy is honoured here so effects need no host knowledge.
Compilation is separated from traversal, so plan-shape changes do not touch the evaluator's execution loop.
State is a struct of five raw Maps owned by the engine and mutated in place by the pure evaluator; any new per-node state means adding a field here and a matching private map + clear() in engine.ts.
Node kinds are handled by branches inside one ~320-line traversal; there is no per-kind handler seam, so adding a node type edits the hot function.
A new modulation source requires coordinated edits in sampleSource, MOD_SOURCE_KINDS, the ModSource union, nodeModSource, and the engine's live table plumbing — five places for one concept.
Optional callback lets hosts observe engine decisions without the engine importing any IO.
Hit→emission lifecycle is shared and host-agnostic; effects opt in by composing it.
A correctness-relevant policy is a per-call option rather than a resolved decision, so different callers can pick different semantics for the same graph.
Descriptions/tags/deprecations are injected by the registry, so 49 impl files stay untouched when copy changes.
Two graph analyses with identical input/output shape and no common lint interface — a third lint has nothing to register against.
No shared effect-conformance harness; each batch re-creates model/framebuffer/context scaffolding, which is where jscpd's largest clone cluster sits.

suspicions.hunch: One ~400-line method appears to hold input normalization, section/pad graph resolution, cc/osc/note table updates, action execution and pending-fire scheduling; several unrelated reasons to change converge on it.
The lettered batch split looks arbitrary and each case likely repeats the same model+framebuffer+ctx setup; a single conformance harness plus a table would probably delete most of the 57 clones.
NodeKind is switched on in at least two places (plan categorisation and traversal); a new node kind probably needs both edited in step, with nothing enforcing it.
ccKey/ccValue01/sampleCc, oscValue01/sampleOsc, and noteKey/noteValue01/sampleNote are three near-identical table-source trios that could be one parameterised source-table abstraction.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/voice/engine.ts private maps (seqIndex, lastPick, latched, mixMemberSnapshots) and eval-graph EvalState
suspicions.hunch: Per-node graph state is spread across four raw Map<string,…> keyed by a hand-built `${prefix}#${nodeId}` string; a missed clear() on one map on setShow would be invisible.
{timeMs, bpm/transport, cc, osc, notes} travels together through compositor → applyEffectiveParams → sampleSource under three different type names.
A legacy-vs-mapping parity comparison harness ships as public API; if the legacy path is gone this is a test fixture living in production exports.
Two migration layers for legacy shapes run on every setShow; if no persisted show still carries the old shapes, this is permanent cost for a finished migration.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/effects/impl/ (42 of 49 files not using emitter.ts)
suspicions.hunch: Only 7 effects compose the emitter substrate; the hit-tracking and hue/velocity param-reading preamble is likely re-derived independently across the rest.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/effects/registry.ts imports '../canvas/presets' for side effect and branches on isCanvasEffectId
suspicions.hunch: The effects registry knows about the canvas subsystem specifically, rather than canvas registering itself into a general provider list — an import-order-sensitive coupling.
Two distinct types share a name across the two halves of this scope and both describe effect parameters; conversion or drift between them is a likely defect site.
Mixed `export *` and curated named exports means the public surface of the voice package is accidental in places; some internals are probably reachable that were never intended to be.
The plan cache keys on a derived string; if the signature omits a field the traversal reads, a mutated graph would silently reuse a stale plan.

When the cap is hit the loop breaks after already advancing lastSeq for earlier triggers, so a burst may drop hits silently with no diagnostic; worth checking the lastSeq bookkeeping on the break path.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/effects/registry.ts module-level `throw new Error('Duplicate effect id')`
suspicions.hunch: A registry-construction failure throws at import time in a pure package, so any duplicate id takes down module loading rather than surfacing as a validation result.

items.coverage_notes: Read in full or substantially: voice/index.ts, voice/engine.ts (header + interface + first 200 lines + method index), voice/eval-graph.ts (export/function index only), effects/types.ts, effects/registry.ts, effects/emitter.ts, compositor.ts (interface + factory head), impl/orbit-comet.ts. For the remaining voice modules I read the exported-symbol index and file headers, not full bodies — so responsibilities are inferred from names, doc comments and import graphs, and could be wrong in detail. NOT read: the bodies of eval-graph.ts (lines 277-594, the core traversal), engine.ts lines 200-850 (applyInput/tick/stats bodies), voice/types.ts beyond its first ~200 lines, metadata.ts contents, and 48 of 49 effects/impl files (mapped as one module from the import histogram and one representative). All test files were mapped from filenames and the supplied jscpd context only — I did not open any test file, so the duplication suspicion there is tooling-derived, not verified. impl/ LOC is an estimate (total scope minus files I counted individually). Cross-scope dependencies (canvas/*, geometry/*, color/*, math, engine/framebuffer, engine/render-context) were treated as external and not inspected.
